name: orlan
author: invented board game (lateral direction)
description:
INVENTED BOARD GAME (v2 - softened after iteration 1). Clue: a small position (5x5..6x6)
drawn with '.' empty, 'o' your pieces, 'x' enemy pieces, '#' immovable blocks. Answer: one
move "r,c>r,c", 0-indexed row,col (the scorer accepts any four integers in order).

HIDDEN RULES. (1) STEP LENGTH: a piece's step n is the number of its four orthogonal
neighbours that hold a piece - 'o', 'x' or '#'. The board rim does NOT count (v1 counted
it; that clause is gone). A piece with n = 0 cannot move at all. (2) MOVE: it leaps
exactly n squares in one of the four orthogonal directions, flying over whatever lies
between (empty squares and pieces alike); the landing square must be on the board and
empty. (3) You move an 'o'. (4) GOAL: after your move no 'x' may have a legal move under
the very same rule - every 'x' is either isolated (step 0) or has all four of its landing
squares off-board or occupied.

WHAT CHANGED FROM v1 AND WHY. In iteration 1 both Opus teams settled on "an 'o' hops along
a line to the FIRST EMPTY cell" and never reached the step-length law; 67 % of v1 winning
moves happened to satisfy that model, so it survived ~2,700 probes and 6 demos and they
finished at ~30 % with learned rankers. v2 makes that model impossible: the winning move
now ALWAYS flies over at least one empty square (measured: 0.0 % of winners land on the
first empty cell along their ray, was 67.4 %), its length is 2 or 3 (never 1, so "it just
steps to a neighbour" is out too), and 37 % of winners also fly over an occupied square,
which kills "the path must be clear". The rim clause was dropped so that the step length
is now readable straight off the picture: count the pieces touching the mover.

Intended path: demo 1 gives the format and kills "first empty cell"; demos 2-3 show a
2-leap and a 3-leap over open ground, and the only thing that differs between the movers
is how many pieces touch them; the goal is then the only simple predicate that makes the
demonstrated move the unique winner among the legal moves.

GENERATION is reverse: build a random position in which no 'x' can move (blocks are added
to repair mobile ones), then un-move one 'o' by n squares, padding the origin with blocks
until its neighbour count is exactly n. Every clue is then verified by enumeration.

WITNESS LEAKS CLOSED. Exactly one move on the whole board wins. >= 7 legal 'o' moves
(mean 9.7), so knowing the law and guessing uniformly pays ~12 %. The generator rejects a
position when the winner is the unique longest move, the unique move landing nearest an
enemy, the only move landing beside an enemy, the only move whose mover touches an enemy,
or - the new v2 filter - one of fewer than five moves that fly over empty ground (that
last one otherwise handed out 37 % for free, since the winner always flies over a gap).
Measured over 700 fresh clues: best of 16 cheap non-rule heuristics 20.4 %, the iteration-1
player model 0.1 %, uniform guess among legal moves 12.1 %.
